stem.en: Carbon dioxide is one carbon and two oxygens. Kabir says it is "one-third carbon by mass, because one atom out of three". What is the mass share of carbon?

text.en: 12 out of 44, about 27 percent. One carbon at 12 plus two oxygens at 16 each makes 44.

feedback.en: Atoms do not weigh the same. Oxygen is heavier than carbon, so two oxygens are more than two-thirds of the mass.
There are two oxygens and one carbon, and each oxygen is heavier than the carbon.

text.en: It cannot be known without a balance.

feedback.en: The relative masses are already known. The arithmetic gives the share without any weighing.

explanation.en: Add up the atoms by their relative masses. Then take the share. The count of atoms and the share of mass are different things.
